reels.caption:
A famous samurai, nearing the end of his life, began to wonder whether heaven and hell truly existed. He was told of a Zen Master named Hakuin who might have the answer.

After climbing a mountain in search of him, the samurai noticed a man sitting quietly on a log of wood.

“Hey, you,” the samurai demanded, drawing his attention. “I need to know — is there really such a thing as heaven and hell?”

Hakuin looked at him calmly and asked, “Who are you?” The warrior replied proudly, “I am the chief samurai to the Emperor.”

Hakuin laughed and said, “You? A samurai? With a face like that? You can’t understand — you look stupid.” The samurai became so angry he drew his sword, ready to strike.

Hakuin stood there unmoving, calm, and said, “Here… the gates of hell open.”

Perceiving the master’s composure, the warrior suddenly became aware of himself, lowered his sword, and bowed.

Hakuin then said, “and here open the gates of heaven.”

***At any moment, - Life, is up to us the way it is created!

reels.caption:
Many of us didn’t receive the love and attention we needed growing up. For some, this lack of love creates a subconscious decision to become someone different—someone they believe will be deserving of love. In codependency language, this is called the “protective self”: a persona that strives to be successful, accomplished, or worthy enough to finally earn love and acceptance. 
When children grow up with emotionally immature or, in some cases, abusive parents, they often experience emotional neglect. This causes them to abandon their own needs and focus on caring for their parents instead of learning to trust and value themselves. Later in life, this pattern makes feelings of calm, serenity, self-trust, and comfort in their own body feel foreign and undeserving. 
I’m ready to offer support to people who need more confidence and recognition of who they truly are. If you—or someone you know—could benefit from this support, please visit aliveawake.org, scroll to the bottom for my contact number, and reach out via WhatsApp. I want to support you!

reels.groupKey: i have condensed the most important lessons i’ve learned in
reels.title: I have condensed the most important lessons I’ve learned in the past 20 years about rel…
reels.caption:
I have condensed the most important lessons I’ve learned in the past 20 years about relationships into this summary.
1. Attachment leads to suffering. Clinging desperately to a person or relationship attaches you to an illusion that will inevitably change or dissolve, leaving you disappointed.
2. Relationships cannot make you happy. True happiness comes from within. Relying on others for happiness gives them control over your inner state.
3. Conflict, even in harmonious relationships, is inevitable. Accepting this allows for constructive resolution rather than emotional turmoil.
4. Love is not a feeling; it is a choice. While infatuation may initially sweep us away, true love is consciously committing even through challenges.
5. Intimacy requires vulnerability. Emotional openness is risky but necessary for meaningful connection. Hiding your authentic self prevents closeness.
6. Relationships can mirror unhealed wounds, providing opportunities for self-awareness, healing, and forgiveness.
7. We cannot fix or rescue others. Our role is to love and support unconditionally, allowing them to find their own path.
8. Relationships reflect our relationship with ourselves. How we treat ourselves sets the tone for how we interact.
9. Relationships involve surrendering and taking responsibility for choices. Find the balance between the two.
10. Relationships are a journey, not a destination. There is no perfect relationship, only evolving, transformative experiences.
Let me know if you have come to know this already!

reels.title: Everybody tells you what you should do.
reels.caption:
Everybody tells you what you should do.

Your parents, your friends, your teachers.

You listen, and act.

Throughout the process, you might wonder: Am I going to be a copycat of my parents, the people I know? Or—is there something else?

If you’ve raised this question, you have experienced the first glimpse of conscious awareness.

To live consciously is not to move on autopilot in your life, but to take intelligent action that stems from the present moment—not the past.

Ever wondered if there was something beyond what you experience as life? Well—there is. ‘Life is not what it appears to be,’ as Eckhart Tolle wrote in his book.

There is more to your life, and you know it. More joy, more ecstasy, more freedom, more depth. It is accessible to you, too.

I can tell you because I was once in your place. Seeking. Wondering. Is there more? What is that ‘more’? Is it in financial abundance? Business? Women?

Sometime in my early 20s, after years of wondering, I came across a master who said, ‘Yes—there is. You are on the right path; keep going—there is a lot more beyond what you’ve tasted.’

I was filled with joy hearing it. Happiness. I had finally come across someone who didn’t try to stop me, cool me off, or cut my growing thrill. But someone who was willing to show me the way, support my evolution, my blossoming.

I was thankful and said yes. Yes to more. Yes to all. Yes to the ultimate experience.

The new man is out there. Follow @selfdiscoveryjourney__ if you want to learn the way to becoming one.

reels.caption:
An awakened man is someone who:

1) Takes full responsibility for his life - a man who recognizes reality for what it truly is understands that his life is his own creation, and he alone holds responsibility for it.

2) Does not blame his partner, country, or anyone else for his circumstances - an awakened man understands the complexities of life. He respects each individual and recognizes the absurdity of the unconscious mind. By being present, he elevates the consciousness of those around him without casting blame or judgment.

3) Realizes that humankind is one united species at its core, undivided by religion or nationality - human beings are fundamentally the same. An awakened man acknowledges this, enabling him to relate to anyone, transcending artificial distinctions and divisions.

4) Lives in the Here and Now, understanding it as the only real moment. The future or past is but a memory. Giving your full attention to the present ensures the next moment will be taken care of.

5) Has no fear of death for he understands eternity. Life extends beyond our physical form, and an awakened man recognizes his eternal nature.

6) Radiates presence, which is palpable when you’re around him. When you encounter such conscious individual, you can sense the depth of his presence and feel his vibrational energy. The more conscious he becomes, the more intense the radiance.

7) Creates and nourishes life, rather than dividing or destroying it. As one becomes more conscious, there’s an inherent drive to support life, to encourage its growth and development. Such an individual acts in the spirit of creation and nurturing, never in destruction.

reels.title: You have a choice to make:
reels.caption:
You have a choice to make:

1.
a. Follow the casual paradigm- Conform to what’s common and accepted.
b. Do what you are being told - Let others dictate your actions without questioning.
c. Hide who you are - Suppress your true self in favor of fitting in.
d. Be like the people around you - Imitate to belong, even if it doesn’t resonate with your essence.
e. Be politically correct - Always say what’s expected, even if it’s not your genuine belief.
f. Survive - Just get by without truly thriving or pursuing passion.

2.
a. Be curious - Keep an inquisitive mind, always seeking deeper insight and understanding.
b. Respect your feelings - Honor your emotions; they’re a true reflection of your experience.
c. Respect your insights - Value your inner wisdom and unique understanding.
d. Act upon what seems true, not what others think - Trust your instincts and be authentic.
e.  Be whole; say no to becoming a hypocrite - Be consistent in your wisdom and actions.
f. Live joyfully - Embrace the beauty of life and find happiness in each moment.

What do you choose?
